body:
Scope question is in #4332 (this changes a default, and CONTRIBUTING.md asks for agreement first). Happy to turn it
into an opt-in or move the boundary on request, and `STRATA_Q36_CHUNK=2048` gives today's chunk either way.

The change itself is one block in the hybrid branch of the chunk rule plus the prompt-chunk section of
`docs/QWEN36.md`.

## Problem and result

With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL on a 16 GB card, the q36 engine's hybrid mode picks the prompt chunk with a fixed
rule (2048 above 7.5 GiB free, 1024 above 5.5, else 512) and never tries 4096. A prompt chunk streams every layer's
experts over PCIe once, so a 4096-token prompt pays that cost per chunk, not per token. Measuring the two arms on the
same binary (RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, WSL2, i7-14700KF, engine 0.1.52 at 5e8a4cc, CUDA 12.4, `--mtp 2`, three
alternating runs per arm, medians):

| cells | chunk | prompt tok/s | prompt ms (runs) | decode tok/s | experts in VRAM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 | 2048 | 840 | 4,830 / 4,872 / 4,885 | 61.9 | 79 / 256 |
| 8192 | 4096 | **1,272** | 3,224 / 3,208 / 3,218 | 61.8 | 66 / 256 |
| 32768 | 2048 | 779 | 5,256 / 5,370 / 5,032 | 51.7 | 63 / 256 |
| 32768 | 4096 | **1,372** | 3,120 / 2,847 / 2,852 | 54.1 | 50 / 256 |
| 16384 (8,192-token prompt) | 2048 | 857 | 10,366 / 9,485 | 45.3 | 63 / 256 |
| 16384 (8,192-token prompt) | 4096 | **1,410** | 5,645 / 5,985 | 47.7 | 50 / 256 |

So: prompt reading 51% faster at 8K context, 76% faster at 32K (4.9 s -> 3.2 s and 5.3 s -> 2.9 s for a 4096-token
prompt), and 64% faster at 16K with an 8,192-token prompt (10.4 s -> 5.6 s); decode unchanged at 8K, and 4-6%
faster at 32K/16K, where the MTP drafts were accepted more often.

## Approach

In the hybrid branch, take 4096 when the chunk's buffers fit in a third of the room the expert slots keep at a
512-token chunk; otherwise keep today's rule:

```
room = fr_raw - 2.97 GiB - ctx * n_attn * n_head_kv * head_dim * 8
chunk = 4096 if (4096 - 512) * 0.5 MiB <= room / 3
```

- 0.5 MiB per token is the measured growth of the chunk's buffers (0.47 MiB at these sizes).
- 2.97 GiB is the engine's buffers at 512, the staging pair and the 0.77 GiB reserve, measured at 8192 and 32768
  cells.
- The K / V term keeps a long context on 2048: at 65536 cells the rule chooses 2048 (4.89 GiB free after init,
  41 experts per layer), which is the arm 0.1.52 runs today.
- A 12 GB card keeps 2048: the chunk's buffers would take most of its slots' room, where docs/QWEN36.md measured a
  13% decode loss for 4096 on an RTX 3060.
- `--batch` keeps the smaller chunk (the 4096 arm runs only with one slot).

The diff is the rule, its comment, and the prompt-chunk section of docs/QWEN36.md.

## Validation

Passed (RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04, driver 581.80, CUDA 12.4 build for sm_89 + sm_61):

- Built `main` at 5e8a4cc with and without the change; the same binary with `--chunk 2048` and with the new rule,
  three alternating runs per arm at 8192 and 32768 cells (table above).
- New rule chooses 4096 at 8192 and 32768 cells and 2048 at 65536 cells (`STRATA_Q36_PLACE_DEBUG=1` shows the
  inputs: free 11.50 GiB, raw 9.72, experts 18.29 GiB).
- The model loads and runs on the 11 GB GTX 1080 Ti (sm_61) with the change too, and that card keeps its old chunk:
  its free VRAM is below 7.5 GiB, so the rule picks 1024 as before and the new arm does not apply (23 experts per
  layer, 34 tok/s decode; that card is not used in the numbers above).
- `ctest` with `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON` on this build (sm_61 + sm_89, CUDA 12.4): 201 of 205 pass. The 4 failures are
  environment/build-configuration ones, none in code this change touches — `ple_parity` (the Qwen3.8 PLE shard fixture
  is not on this machine), `platform_memory_test` (a host-memory heuristic sized for a larger guest than this 24 GB
  WSL one), `isa_guard_check` (an AVX-512 function is not on this build's allowlist) and `cuda_spill_guard` (the
  stack-use allowlist does not cover sm_61/sm_89 with this toolkit).

Not run:

- 12 GB and 8 GB cards; the boundary there is arithmetic from the measured 0.5 MiB/token and the RTX 3060 line in
  the docs, not a measurement.
- HIP, SYCL, Metal and Windows builds (the change is device-neutral host code in `strata::qwen35::run`).
- `--batch` / parallel requests beyond compiling the `batch > 1` guard.

## Limits

- The chunk size changes the GEMM tiles the BLAS picks, so the text differs in its last bits from the 2048 arm. This
  is the difference docs/QWEN36.md already describes for every chunk size except 512; the change does not touch
  kernels, routing, precision or the KV cache.
- The gain is prompt-side (time to first token). Decode follows the experts' placement and is unchanged at 8K; at 32K
  it moved +4.6% here, but I would not quote that as a decode improvement.

Fixes #4332 once the scope is agreed.
title: [Engine] q36: a 4096-token prompt chunk in the hybrid mode when the card has room
head: q36-hybrid-chunk-4096
